title: games-market
line: A test bench and catalogue of web games for live events: the projector is the screen and people's phones are the controllers.

facts.v: Star-shaped WebRTC, the projector as host

film.alt: Ninja in full screen: coloured shapes fly up from below and the slice splits them while the score goes up.
film.label: Lab · Canvas 2D

ten.v: Seeing how each game looks and plays took a real session with a room code, and there were 24 planned.
A bench that opens any game instantly, with seed, simulated latency and loss, «Force end» and FPS in view.
18 playable: 6 stable and 12 in beta, including the three 3D ones. The bench serves to build them and to show them.

how.d: The container sets room, seed, duration, seat, host and network.
Each phone joins through a QR and opens a direct channel to the projector.
Seeded PRNG and Rapier physics: the same seed gives the same match.
Snapshots delta-encoded against the last confirmed tick, with interpolation and prediction.
onFinish fires exactly once; if aborted, it delivers the partial result.

decisions.why: Seeded PRNG and Rapier compiled to WASM: the same seed gives the same match, and that is what makes the netcode possible.
WebRTC with PeerJS and the projector as the single authority; in development, BroadcastChannel links two tabs and the games stay unaware.

decisions.t: Each game in its own chunk
decisions.why: Rapier weighs 2.1 MB in 2D and 2.2 MB in 3D: only whoever opens a game that uses it downloads it.

arena-3d.alt: 3D aerial view of a green valley with hills and houses under a sunset sky, the closing ring and the player markers.
arena-3d.caption: 3D arena: aerial view of the valley with ten bot players.

catalogo.alt: Dark "Batería de experiencias" catalogue with game cards, each with topology, engine and status, plus the side list by category.
catalogo.caption: The bench catalogue, with category and topology filters.

more.p: The 24 games were ordered into 12 batches by a score from 0 to 18 across six axes. Work can stop at any batch and the product still serves; the 3D ones came last.
Football was the first to use the whole snapshot layer, and it found five problems. With 20% simulated loss: 121 packets lost and zero decoding failures.
814 pure-logic unit tests in 39 files: games, engines, network, contract and interface. CI runs lint, tests and build before publishing.

next: Next step: trying the networked games on real phones, at an event.
